{
  "description": "OAuth2 Proxy is a reverse proxy and middleware component that provides authentication via OAuth2/OIDC providers. It intercepts HTTP requests, redirects users to an identity provider for login, validates tokens (JWT/OIDC), and forwards authenticated requests to upstream services with user claims in HTTP headers. It also supports basic authentication via htpasswd files.",

      "confidence": 0.95,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "README.md@39ec0e19",
        "oauthproxy.go@39ec0e19",
        "pkg/authentication/basic/htpasswd.go@39ec0e19"
      ],
      "notes": "Provides robust authentication via OIDC/OAuth2 providers and basic auth. Handles session management, token validation, and user identity extraction."

    "Linux/Windows/macOS",

  "deployment_constraints": [
    "Requires network access to OIDC/OAuth2 identity providers",
    "Requires TLS termination or reverse proxy setup for secure header forwarding",
    "Containerized deployment recommended (distroless base image)"
  ],
  "maturity": "stable",
  "adaptation_hours_estimate": 40,
  "adaptation_confidence": "medium",
  "adaptation_assumptions": [
    "Assumes existing OIDC/OAuth2 identity provider is available",
    "Assumes upstream application can accept authentication headers",
    "Configuration will be managed via environment variables or config files"
  ],
  "known_gaps": [
    "No native MQTT support for configuration distribution",
    "No built-in geofencing capabilities",
    "No dynamic policy engine (static configuration only)",
    "No user role/permission management UI or API (relies on upstream)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "MIT License is permissive but lacks patent protection",
    "Volunteer-driven project may have variable response times for security issues",
    "Complex OIDC provider configurations can be error-prone",
    "No built-in audit logging for authentication events"
  ],
  "evidence": [
